Namibia: Law and Practice

Contributed by SNC Inc. Last updated: 06 August 2026

1. General Structure of Hydrocarbon Ownership and Regulation

1.1 System of Petroleum Ownership

Under Article 100 of the Namibian Constitution, land, water and natural resources below and above the surface of the land belong to the State if they are not otherwise lawfully owned. The Petroleum (Exploration and Production) Act 2 of 1991 vests all rights in relation to petroleum in the State.

1.2 Regulatory Bodies

The Ministry of Industries, Mines and Energy, through its Petroleum Affairs Directorate, administers the Act. The Petroleum Commissioner is the statutory officer under the Act. The National Petroleum Corporation of Namibia (NAMCOR) holds a carried interest in every licence.

1.3 National Oil or Gas Company

NAMCOR holds a 10% carried interest during exploration in each petroleum agreement entered into since 2015.

2. Private Investment in Hydrocarbons: Upstream

2.1 Forms of Private Investment

Private investment in the upstream sector is by way of a reconnaissance licence, an exploration licence or a production licence granted under the Act, together with a petroleum agreement with the Government.

2.2 Issuing Upstream Licences

Namibia has operated an open licensing system since 1999. An application is made to the Minister in duplicate, and the terms are negotiated by an inter-ministerial negotiating team.

2.5 Fiscal Terms

The Petroleum (Taxation) Act 3 of 1991 provides for a royalty of 5% of the gross value of petroleum produced, petroleum income tax at 35% and an additional profits tax calculated on the after-tax net cash flow of the licence area.

3. Foreign Investment

There are no general restrictions on foreign ownership of a licence interest, although the Minister may require Namibian participation.

4. EHS

The Environmental Management Act 7 of 2007 requires an environmental clearance certificate before exploration or production operations begin.
